origin: Named for a sheet of paper rising from the bottom of the screen. Google's Material Design defined the term.
whenToUse: People choose one of a few options, such as a sort order or who to share with.
You gather actions for an item (edit, delete, share) while keeping the current screen.
You want choices within easier reach than the top of a mobile screen.
whenNotToUse: It needs a long multi-step input or long text.
You must get confirmation for something that can't be undone.
It's a menu used with a mouse on a wide screen (a dropdown menu opens closer).

alternatives.name: Modal Dialog
alternatives.reason: When people should focus on an important decision and its effect.

alternatives.name: Drawer
alternatives.reason: Long filters or details from the side of the screen.

alternatives.name: Dropdown Menu
alternatives.reason: A list of actions right under a button on desktop.

accessibility: Open it with the native <dialog> showModal() to trap focus in the panel and make the background inert.
Connect the title with aria-labelledby so screen readers announce the panel's purpose first.
Esc, a tap on the backdrop, or a visible close button all close it, so swiping isn't the only way.
The rising animation turns off with prefers-reduced-motion.
